page: Amazon Web Services i2.2xlarge is a storage-optimized second-generation instance utilizing the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is 61.0 GB, providing 7.62 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 1600 GB NVMe SSD, and the baseline network bandwidth is 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate average performance in several areas alongside notable limitations. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests score in the average range at 1619.98 and 7138.99 respectively. However, Geekbench scores are poor, with a single-core score of 529.0 and a multi-core score of 2015.0. Memory bandwidth is mixed; read-only large block bandwidth is average at 40.1 GB/sec, whereas write large block bandwidth is weak at 19.3 GB/sec. Cryptographic performance is stable, with a PassMark CPU encryption score of 3694.94, which is in the average tier.

The primary tradeoff of the i2.2xlarge is its older processor architecture, which lacks AVX-512 and AMX instructions, resulting in poor performance for modern workloads like LLM text generation and Redis SET operations. However, the inclusion of 1600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 61.0 GB of RAM makes it suitable for legacy database operations, static web serving averaging 7.59 GB/sec throughput, and workloads requiring high local storage capacity without demanding state-of-the-art CPU compute.
